review.head: 9a27ea19ef03f1993871e5bc98e37a2ab4877555
checks: Read scripts/agy_runner.py worktree_digest source directly: names come from ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, NUL-split, deduped/sorted; new guard `if not path.is_symlink() and (not path.exists() or path.is_dir()): continue` drops (a) deleted/otherwise-missing index entries and (b) real directories, while symlinks always proceed because is_symlink() is checked first. Correct fix for file-to-directory replacement: pre-commit a tracked path naming a real directory is skipped, post-commit the directory is untracked-but-empty (ls-files lists directories only for tracked files, so nothing is yielded) and its tracked leaf children are hashed identically; observed by reasoning over ls-files semantics since coordinator gate log is cited, not run by me.

Symlink detection preserved: is_symlink() links, including dangling ones, hash name + b'link:' + os.readlink() raw target; dangling links to missing/directory targets are not collapsed by exists()/is_dir(); regression test_symlink_snapshots_survive_commit_and_detect_retargeting creates start.md->link-target, file-link.md->link-target/one.md deflecting to a same-content two.md, and dangling-link.md absent-one->absent-two, asserting digest inequality on each retarget and equality after restore, plus ledger.submit raising 'snapshot' after committing a '.' retarget.

Deletion and rename detection preserved: removed paths now skipped (is_dir not reached; exists False) and digest equals post-commit state where they are absent; test_deleted_file_snapshot_survives_commit and test_renamed_file_snapshot_survives_commit still exist unchanged and submit successfully; test_submit_rejects_changes_after_model_execution still asserts coordinator content edits fail submit.

Coordinator edit detection for directory replacement is exercised end-to-end: test_directory_replacement_snapshot_survives_commit_and_rejects_edits asserts digest stable across git add and commitStatus changes, submits to 'review', then overwrites docs/start.md/nested/child.md, commits, and asserts Error 'snapshot' — plausible because submit compares runs[-1]['worktree_digest'] from the succeeded execute receipt (agy_runner.py sets record['worktree_digest']=worktree_digest(worktree) before state='succeeded') against a fresh worktree_digest(task['worktree']) for runtime_managed tasks (agentctl.py submit); digest includes path name + execute-bit + sha256 of content for each leaf, so changed child content changes it.

Child-edit detection verified from hashing logic: for each Git-visible leaf a file, digest mixes name, stat execute bit and sha256(path.read_bytes()); symlinks mix readlink target. Files under a real directory (untracked ones and tracked descendants) are individually enumerated by ls-files --others/--cached, so an edit cannot be hidden.

Filesystem reading limitation: I could not execute Python/Git; I verified the fixture script's shell block for kinds 'directory' and 'symlink' (unlink docs/start.md, mkdir start.md/nested with child.md, symlink fixtures) reads as syntactically coherent and the test logic is consistent with the fixture behavior expected. No reproducible defect identified from the source; no claim made that the tests passed for me.

Regression is meaningful and placed in the owning test file (scripts/test_agy_runner.py, included in the verify gate); test_original_directory_replacement_probe_is_stable consumes the same scripts/evolution.py snapshot_probe discovery predicate (git init, file->dir, digest before/after commit, require stable) as an in-tree regression rather than a reimplemented copy, and the probe's state='stable' compares pre/post-commit output without environmental influence, so it is not vacuous.

Docs change (docs/subsystems/coordination.md) states the verified semantics: Git-visible paths/content/exec bit/symlink targets, links not followed (dangling and directory-target links included), deleted or directory-replaced old paths skipped, descendants still checked, deletion/rename/dir-replacement snapshot stability, coordinator child or link-target edits failing submit — consistent with the implementation and tests.

Checks honesty: unit tests, verify.sh (test_verify, test_agentctl, test_agy_runner, test_runtime_adapters, test_evolution, cargo fmt/clippy/test/build/deny) and a real agy run were not executed by me; only file reads were possible. Known non-blocking preferences previously raised (retaining the successful Ledger.submit state=='review' assertion) were not treated as defects per instruction, since this exact submitted implementation is what is being judged and successful submit after file-to-directory replacement is a substantive end-to-end assertion.
